data.current_description: Use a compatible MCP client. Send one UTF-8 JSON-RPC object per POST with Content-Type: application/json and Accept: application/json, text/event-stream. Protocol negotiation supports 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25; the SDK manages version metadata and headers. Successful protocol requests return JSON or finite SSE depending on the negotiated protocol. Tool failures can have HTTP 200 and result.isError=true; ask_doctor with label_amount=null is a successful reference lookup. GET and DELETE are unsupported (405), and cross-origin browser access is not enabled. Bodies are limited to 16384 bytes; batches are rejected; function execution is limited to ten seconds. The hosting firewall limits /api/mcp to 120 HTTP requests per IP per 60-second fixed window in each region, across methods and hostnames. All MCP HTTP methods and protocol messages count, including initialization, notifications and tool calls. Shared networks, NAT gateways and MCP providers share the same IP cap. Counters are regional, not a single worldwide quota. Excess requests return HTTP 429 at the hosting firewall before reaching the application. A 429 response may be HTML rather than JSON. Honor a valid Retry-After value when present; otherwise wait at least 60 seconds. Use exponential backoff with jitter and a bounded number of retries. Do not retry immediately or switch IP addresses to evade the cap. Application MCP responses include RateLimit-Policy: "mcp-ip-region";q=120;w=60;qu="requests". This informational policy header follows the current IETF HTTPAPI draft, not a finalized RFC; it does not report remaining requests or a reset time. The application cannot read the firewall's counters, so it does not emit a RateLimit remaining/reset value. The policy header is not guaranteed on firewall-blocked responses. Never send patient details.

Accepts Content-Type: application/json with response as JSON or Server-Sent Events (SSE). Supports protocol versions 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25. Tool execution is limited to 10 seconds per request. Rate limited to 120 requests per IP per 60-second window per region; excess requests return HTTP 429. Successful responses include result.isError=true for tool failures (e.g., ask_doctor with label_amount=null indicates successful reference lookup). Never include patient names, medical history, or exact measurements in requests. Request bodies limited to 16384 bytes; batches not supported. On rate limit, honor Retry-After header or wait 60+ seconds before retrying with exponential backoff.
